Its authenticity even as a mawquf is open to question, for its narrator from Ibn Jurayj and al-Awza'i is Amr ibn Harun, who is not strong. Yahya ibn Abi Unaysa also narrated it from Amr ibn Shu'ayb with this chain as a mawquf, and he is abandoned (matruk). We only argue with the narrations of Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather when the one who narrates from him is trustworthy (thiqah) and there is added to it something that confirms it. We have not found a sound chain for this hadith to Amr. And Allah knows best. End of his words, and end of the words of the author of *Nasb al-Raya*.

The author of *al-Jawhar al-Naqi* said: The hadith mentioned is of good chain (jayyid al-isnad). Even if we assume its chain is good as he mentioned, it does not follow from that that the testimonies of li'an are testimonies and not oaths, because it is possible that the absence of mula'anah among those mentioned in the hadith is due to the lack of equality (al-mukafa'ah).

What appears more correct to us is that they are oaths that have been emphasized by the wording of testimony, on account of the evidences we have mentioned. This is the view of the majority of scholars. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

**Third issue:** Know that in li'an it is not permissible to rely on the wife giving birth to a black child when she and her husband are both fair-skinned. This is due to the case of the man whose wife bore a black boy, and he informed the Prophet (ﷺ), as if alluding to disowning the black child through li'an. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Do you have camels?" He said: Yes. He said: "What colour are they?" He said: Red. He said: "Are there any grey ones among them?" He said: Indeed there are some greyish ones. He said: "From where did the greyness come to them?" He said: Perhaps a hereditary strain pulled them. He said: "Likewise, this black boy may have a hereditary strain that pulled him." The story is well known and firmly established in the two *Sahihs*, and we have presented it many times. In it is the evidence that the blackness of the child cannot be a basis for the man in li'an, as you see.

* *

**Fourth issue:** Know that the verified position is that whoever slanders a woman with fornication before he marries her, and then marries her, if he does not produce four witnesses to her fornication, he is flogged with the hadd of slander (hadd al-qadhf, the prescribed punishment for slander), and li'an is not accepted from him. This is because at the time of the slander she was a non-related (ajnabiyyah), chaste (muhsanah) woman, included in the general meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. The marriage that occurs after that does not change the ruling established before it. What is related from Imam Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him), that if he slandered her before marriage and then married her after the slander, the two perform li'an, is contrary to the apparent meaning of the noble verse according to us. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

**Fifth issue:** Know that the verified position is that if a husband slanders his wife and her mother with fornication, and he does not bring evidence (al-bayyinah), he is subjected to the hadd of slander for the mother, because he slandered her with fornication while she is chaste and not a wife. She is included in the general meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾, etc. As for the daughter, he performs li'an with her, because he slandered her while she is his wife, so she falls under the general meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is indeed of the truthful﴾, to the end of the verses of li'an.

From what we have mentioned you know that the statement of some imams: if the mother is punished with the hadd, the hadd for the daughter falls away; and if he performs li'an with the daughter, the hadd for the mother does not fall away, is contrary to the verified position that the verses of the Qur'an indicate. Ibn al-Arabi said regarding the aforementioned statement: "This is extremely false, for it specified the generality of the verse concerning the daughter, who is a wife, by the hadd of the mother, without any report or principle on which it is analogised." End of quotation. And this is clear.

* *

**Sixth issue:** Know that what appears to us to be correct is this: whoever slanders his wife with fornication, and then she commits fornication before his li'an, there is no hadd upon him and no li'an, because it became clear by her fornication before the li'an that she is not chaste (muhsanah), and there is no li'an in slandering one who is not chaste. As we previously mentioned, if he slanders a non-related woman with fornication and then she commits fornication before the hadd is carried out on him, the apparent position for us is that the hadd falls away, because it has become clear by her fornication that she was not chaste before the hadd was carried out. So he is not flogged for slandering someone who has been shown not to be chaste. We have mentioned the disagreement on this matter.

The argument of those who say: he is flogged if she was a non-related woman, and performs li'an if she was a wife, is that the hadd and li'an became obligatory at the time of the slander, so they do not fall away due to the subsequent fornication. We have explained that the more apparent position is that the hadd and li'an fall away, because it has become clear that she was not chaste before the hadd and before the li'an. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

**Seventh issue:** Know that whoever throws (accuses) his wife who is elderly and cannot bear children because of her advanced age, the two perform li'an: he to ward off the hadd, and she to avert the punishment. As for if he accuses his young wife who cannot bear children because of her youth, we have previously mentioned the disagreement of the scholars as to whether the hadd of slander is obligatory on him if she is a young girl capable of intercourse but has not reached puberty. According to the view that the hadd is obligatory upon him, it is required of him to perform li'an to ward off the hadd. As for the view that there is no hadd at all for slandering a young girl, there is no li'an upon him for slandering her. We have previously mentioned the position that appears more preponderant to us in this matter. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

**Eighth issue:** Know that if he denies the pregnancy of his wife, the scholars have differed as to whether he may perform li'an with her while she is pregnant, in denying what is in her womb, or whether li'an is not permissible for him until she gives birth to the child. The majority of scholars held that he performs li'an with her while she is pregnant, and his pregnancy is negated by the li'an. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*, after citing the hadiths of li'an, and in it [is the evidence] that a pregnant woman is subjected to li'an before delivery, because of his words in the hadith: "Watch: if she gives birth..." etc., as has preceded in the hadith of Sahl, and in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, and in Muslim's hadith from Ibn Mas'ud: "Then he came, meaning the man, with his wife, and they performed li'an. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Perhaps she will bring him forth black, curly-haired.' Then she brought him forth black, curly-haired." The majority held this, in contrast to those of the school of opinion (ahl al-ra'y) who refused that, arguing that the pregnancy cannot be known, because it may be a swelling (nafkhah).

The majority's argument is that li'an was legislated to ward off the hadd of slander from the man and the hadd of stoning from the woman. Therefore there is no difference between her being pregnant or not pregnant. For this reason li'an was legislated even with a woman past childbearing age.

There has been disagreement concerning a young girl, and the majority hold that if a man slanders her, he may perform li'an to ward off the hadd of slander from himself, but not on her behalf. End of the point of interest from Ibn Hajar's words.

We have previously stated that the li'an of one who slanders a young girl is based on his being subjected to the hadd for slandering her. We have previously presented the words of the scholars and their disagreement concerning the hadd for slandering a young girl who is capable of intercourse, and we mentioned what appears to us to be preponderant in that.

As for those who said: the pregnant woman is not subjected to li'an until she gives birth to her child, they relied on two matters:

The first: pregnancy cannot be certainly known before delivery, because it may be a swelling and it may be wind.

The second: it is what came in some narrations of the hadiths of li'an, which indicates that the Prophet (ﷺ) delayed the li'an of the pregnant woman until she had given birth. In al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, the text is: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, make it clear.' Then she gave birth to one resembling the man whom her husband mentioned he had found with her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed li'an between them..." The hadith. They said: its sequence, *fa-la'ana* (then he performed li'an), with the particle *fa* (then) after his words "she gave birth to one resembling the man," etc., is evidence that the li'an was after the delivery, as the meaning of the *fa* indicates. The majority answered regarding this narration by what Ibn Hajar mentioned in *Fath al-Bari*. He said in his commentary on the narration: its apparent meaning is that the li'an was postponed until the woman gave birth. But he clarified that this narration of Ibn Abbas concerns the story in the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, and it preceded earlier in the hadith of Sahl that the li'an took place between them before she gave birth. Accordingly, the *fa* in his words *fa-la'ana* (then he performed li'an) is connected (mu'aqqibah) to his words "he informed him of what he had found his wife doing," and this sentence, to which Ibn Hajar said the clause *fa-la'ana* is coordinated (ma'tufah), is mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, the place of our point from it.

What appears to us is that the pregnant woman performs li'an before delivery, because of the clear statement of the sound hadiths to that effect, and because of what Ibn Hajar mentioned in his statement which we quoted just now. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

**Ninth issue:** Know that the most apparent of the scholars' positions to me regarding one who divorces his wife and then slanders her after the divorce is this: if his slander consists of denying a pregnancy that was not known to him except after the divorce, he performs li'an with her to deny that pregnancy from himself, even if she is irrevocably divorced (ba'in). And if he slanders her with fornication after the divorce, he is flogged and is not subjected to li'an, because his delaying the slander and li'an until a time after the divorce is evidence that he is a slanderer. And the more apparent position, even if the divorce was revocable (raj'i) and the ʿiddah (waiting period) has not ended, though a revocably divorced woman is in the legal status of a wife, is that his divorcing her before the slander is evidence that he does not intend li'an, and he is flogged. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas. It was said: he performs li'an with the revocably divorced woman before the end of the ʿiddah, because she is in the legal status of a wife. This is the well-known school of Ahmad, the narration of Abu Talib from him, and it was said by Ibn Umar, Jabir, Zayd, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq, Abu Ubayd, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y), and it has a basis in reasoning. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 8 (part 3 of 5):

Al-Qurtubi said: There is no mutual imprecation (li'an) between a man and his wife after the expiry of the waiting period ('iddah), except in one case: when the husband is absent, his wife gives birth to a child during his absence, and he does not know of it. He then divorces her, her 'iddah expires, and afterwards he returns and disowns the child. In this case he may perform li'an against her after the 'iddah. Likewise, if he returns after her death and disowns the child, he performs li'an for himself, while she is dead, after some period of the 'iddah, and he inherits from her, because she died before the separation between them took place. End of quotation from him. There is no explicit text on this, but it has a basis in reasoning.

Al-Qurtubi also said: If he slanders her after the divorce, she is examined. If there is a lineage (nasab) that he wishes to deny, or a pregnancy from which he wishes to disclaim responsibility, he performs li'an. Otherwise, he does not perform li'an. 'Uthman al-Batti said: He never performs li'an in any circumstance. Abu Hanifa said: He does not perform li'an in either of the two cases, because she is no longer a wife. This is refuted by slander that occurs before marriage, as we have mentioned just above. Rather, this case is more deserving of li'an, because the marriage has already taken place and he wishes to deny the lineage and to disclaim a child who would be attributed to him. Therefore li'an is necessary. When there is no expected pregnancy and no lineage feared to be attached, li'an serves no purpose, so it is not prescribed, and the accusation is a general slander falling under the general meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ [al-Nur: 4], so the prescribed punishment (hadd) becomes obligatory for him. The view of al-Batti is void because its corruption is evident. End of al-Qurtubi's words.

We have already mentioned that the view that a revocable divorcee may undergo li'an before the expiry of her 'iddah has a basis in reasoning, because she is in the status of a wife. We have also mentioned what appears to us to be the strongest of the opinions on this and the views of the scholars. The benefit of his li'an is that it averts from him the prescribed punishment for slander. That a revocable divorcee is like a wife before the expiry of the 'iddah means that the two inherit from each other, and he may not marry her sister before the 'iddah expires, nor marry a fourth woman other than her, because she is counted as the fifth. Considering that a revocable divorcee is like a wife, the view that li'an is valid for a revocable divorcee before the expiry of the 'iddah has a basis in reasoning. I have seen many scholars who held this view. The reasoning of those who hold the opposite is that, since he divorced her knowing, in his claim, of her adultery, this indicates that he has abandoned li'an. Based on the disagreement mentioned, there is the case where he claims that she committed adultery after a revocable divorce and before the expiry of the 'iddah. Is he judged to be a slanderer, because he accused her of adultery occurring after the separation, or may he perform li'an against her to remove the prescribed punishment from himself, on the basis that a revocable divorcee is in the status of a wife?

As for if he slandered her before he divorced her, and then divorced her after the slander, then the more evident view is that he may perform li'an against her in every case, even if the divorce was irrevocable (ba'in), because the slander occurred while she was still a wife and not yet divorced. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and it was the view of al-Hasan, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Makhul, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Thawr, and Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Harith al-'Ukli, Jabir ibn Zayd, Qatadah and al-Hakam said: he is flogged. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) said: there is neither prescribed punishment nor li'an, because li'an occurs only between spouses, and these two are not spouses. Nor is he punished, because he did not slander a stranger.

* *

The tenth issue: Know that the most evident of the views of the scholars, in my opinion, concerning a man whose wife has become visibly pregnant, and who says that it is not from him, is this: if he remains silent about denying that pregnancy until she gives birth, and then says that he only remained silent about denying it during the period of pregnancy in the hope that it would be wind or swelling, which would deflate, or that the child would be stillborn, so that he would be relieved of li'an, then he is enabled to deny it by li'an after the birth, because the excuse he has given is weighty and deserves acceptance. If he hastens to deny it immediately upon its birth, there should be no disagreement that he may deny it by li'an. But if he remained silent about denying it after the birth, and then wished to deny it after that silence, is that permitted to him or not? Because his silence after the birth is considered an acceptance on his part of the child, so he is not enabled to perform li'an after it.

I have not found in this issue any explicit text from the Book or the Sunnah, and the scholars differ about it. Al-Qurtubi said: It has been disputed about this, and we say: if he has no excuse for his silence, and three days pass, then he is content with it and he has no right to deny it. This is also the view of al-Shafi'i. He also said: Whenever he could have denied it in the customary manner, by presenting himself to the judge, and he did not do so, he has no right to deny it after that. Abu Hanifa said: I do not consider any period. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: a period of forty days, the period of postnatal bleeding (nifas), shall be considered. Ibn al-Qassar said: The evidence for our view is that denying one's child is forbidden to him, while claiming a child that is not his is forbidden to him. Therefore it is necessary that he be given latitude so that he may consider it and reflect whether it is permitted for him to deny it or not. We made the limit three days because it is the first limit of abundance and the last limit of scarcity, and three days are the period in which the condition of the musharrah (a she-camel or goat whose udder is tied to deceive buyers) is tested, and it should be likewise here. As for Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, their consideration is no more preferable than the consideration of the period of childbirth and suckling, since they have no witness in the Shari'ah. We have mentioned a witness in the Shari'ah from the period of the musharrah. End of al-Qurtubi's words. The weakness of the evidence used by Ibn al-Qassar, one of the Maliki scholars, for limiting it to three days is not hidden.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: This issue is based on a disagreement over a principle of usul al-fiqh, namely: Is silence to be treated as affirmation or not? The author of "Maraqi al-Su'ud" has indicated this, saying:

"Treating one who keeps silent as one who affirms, there is well-known disagreement among them about it.
The argument from silence has flourished, and those before him have built upon it,
and it is fitting, in the absence of anger and its opposite, after the passing of a period for reflection."

Whoever says that silence is not considered acceptance says: because the silent person may keep silent about objecting while not being content. Whoever says that it is considered acceptance says: because his silence is an indication pointing to his consent. They rely on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the virgin: "Her permission is her silence." Some say: singling out the virgin for this indicates that others are not like that. The disagreement in this issue is well known in the branches (furu') and principles (usul) of the Imams. Whoever examines their branches finds that in some cases they treat silence as consent, such as silence regarding li'an for a period after knowledge of its requirement, and silence regarding exercising the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) and the like. The treatment of silence as consent is common in the branches of the Maliki school.

Among the examples of this is what Ibn 'Asim said in his rajaz concerning the rulings of judgeship in the Maliki school:

"One present for a donor of his property, who did not change what he saw of his condition,
the ruling prevents him from rising at the end of the session, since his silence is the very sign of consent."

For each of the two views there is a basis in reasoning.

What appears to us regarding the issue of silence about li'an is that if he remains silent for a period in which, customarily, it is strongly presumed that no one would remain silent except one who is content, then it is considered consent. Otherwise, it is not, because custom is the arbiter. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The eleventh issue: Know that if the marriage is invalid (fasid), and her husband slanders her with adultery, if it is to deny a lineage that would be attached to him through that invalid marriage, then there should be no disagreement that he performs li'an to deny the lineage from himself. But if the invalid marriage is one in which a child is attached to him, yet he slandered her with adultery and wishes to perform li'an to remove the prescribed punishment from himself, then the more evident view is that he may do so, because once she is one to whom the child is attached, she is in the status of the marital bed (firash). This was stated by Malik in the "Mudawwanah."

Al-Qurtubi said: He performs li'an against his wife in an invalid marriage, because she has become a marital bed, and lineage is attached to it in the manner of li'an within it. End of quotation from him.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears to me is that if the invalidity of the marriage is agreed upon, and the child is not attached through it, then the husband who slanders in it is not enabled to perform li'an, but rather is subjected to the prescribed punishment for slander, unless he brings four witnesses. This is evident and not hidden. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The twelfth issue: Know that the most evident of the views of the scholars, in my opinion, concerning a man who slanders his pregnant wife with adultery, and then brings four witnesses to her adultery, is that he may perform li'an to deny the pregnancy alongside the witnesses. This is because the testimony of the witnesses benefits the husband only in averting the prescribed punishment from him. But removing the marital bed and denying the child requires li'an.

Al-Qurtubi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They also disagreed about whether the husband may perform li'an together with his witnesses. Malik and al-Shafi'i said: He performs li'an whether or not he has witnesses, because the witnesses have no role other than averting the prescribed punishment. As for removing the marital bed and denying the child, that requires li'an.

Abu Hanifa and his companions said: li'an is prescribed only when he has no witnesses other than himself, based on His saying: ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves﴾ [al-Nur: 6]. End of quotation from him.

* *

The thirteenth issue: Al-Qurtubi also said in his tafsir: Li'an requires four things: the number of the formulas, which are four testimonies as mentioned above; the place, which is to be chosen as the noblest place in the lands, so if it is in Makkah, then between the Corner (al-Rukn) and the Station (al-Maqam); if it is in Madinah, then at the minbar; if it is in Jerusalem, then at the Rock; and if it is in the rest of the lands, then in their mosques. If the two are disbelievers, they are sent to the place which they believe to be sacred: if they are Jews, then to the synagogue; if they are Magians, then to the fire temple; and if they have no religion, like the idolaters, then the li'an is performed between them in the session of the judge. The time, which is after the 'Asr prayer. The gathering of people, which means that there should be four persons or more. The formula and the gathering of people are conditions, while the time and place are recommended. End of quotation from him. However, the well-known position of the Maliki school, which is the school of al-Qurtubi, is that there is no li'an between disbelievers, and some of what he mentioned is not free from disagreement.

* *

The fourteenth issue: Know that a husband may not deny a child by li'an except for a cause that requires that the child is not from him, such as if the wife committed adultery before the husband had touched her at all; or she committed adultery after she gave birth, and the husband had not touched her after the birth until she committed adultery; or she committed adultery in a period of purity during which he did not touch her. This is because menstruation before the adultery indicates that the pregnancy is from the adultery which occurred after the menstruation. It is not permitted for him to rely, in denying a pregnancy by li'an, on the child's resemblance to another, nor on the child's dark complexion, as we have mentioned. Nor on 'azl (withdrawal), because semen may precede withdrawal and then she conceives from it. Nor on intercourse between the thighs, because the semen flows to the vagina and she conceives from it, as we have mentioned.

* *

The fifteenth issue: Know that any two children between whom there is less than six months are twins, so it is not permitted to deny one of them without the other. If the husband acknowledges one of them, he must accept the other. The evident view is that if he denies one of them while acknowledging the second, he is punished for slander, as stated by Malik and his companions, and those who agree with them.

We have explained in surah al-Ra'd, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase. And everything with Him is in measure﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8], that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, and we mentioned the verses that indicate this. It is known from it that any two children between whom there are less than six months are twins.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: If his wife gives birth to twins, that is, the period between them is less than six months, and he disowns one of them (istalhaqa ahadahuma, i.e., he acknowledges one) and denies the other, both are attributed to him. This is because a single pregnancy cannot have one part of it from him and another part from someone else. So once the lineage of one of them is established from him, the lineage of the other is established by necessity. Thus we made what he denied follow what he acknowledged, and we did not make what he acknowledged follow what he denied, because lineage is guarded toward establishing it, not toward negating it. For this reason, if his wife brings forth a child who could be from him, and could be from someone else, we attribute it to him out of caution, and we do not cut it off from him out of caution for negating it. He continued: If he acknowledges one of the twins and remains silent about the other, it is attributed to him too, because if he had denied it, it would still have been attributed to him, so when he is silent about it, it is more so. Also, whenever his wife bears a child, it is attributed to him so long as he does not negate it from himself by li'an ( li'an: the oath of mutual cursing between spouses). If he denies one and is silent about the other, both are attributed to him.

If it is said: Why do you not negate the one he was silent about, since he has already negated his brother, and they are a single pregnancy?

We say: The attribution of lineage is based on predominance (taghlib), and it is established merely by the possibility (of paternity), even if intercourse was not established, and the possibility is not negated by the denial. So they differ. If she brings forth a child, he denies it, and performs li'an for its negation, then she bears another child less than six months later, the second is not negated by the first li'an, because the li'an applied to the first alone, and to negate the second a second li'an is required. However, it is possible that it is negated by his denial without need for a second li'an, because they are a single pregnancy and he has performed li'an once for its negation, so a second li'an is not needed. This was mentioned by al-Qadi.

The compiler of this commentary, may Allah pardon and forgive him, says: This last view is the more apparent, because a single pregnancy does not require two li'ans. Then Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni, continuing directly from his first statement: If he acknowledges the second, it is attributed to him and to the first for the reason we have mentioned. If he remains silent about denying it, both are attributed to him as well. As for if he denies the child by li'an and then she gives birth to another child after six months, this is from another pregnancy, for it is not possible that the period of pregnancy occurs between two children of a single pregnancy. Even if it were possible, this would not be the period of a complete pregnancy. If he denies this child by li'an, it is negated, and it is not negated without li'an, because it is a separate pregnancy. If he acknowledges it or leaves off negating it, it is attributed to him, even if she has been separated from him by li'an, because it is possible that he had intercourse with her after the delivery of the first. If he performed li'an with her before the delivery of the first, and she then bore a child, and then bore another after six months, the second is not attributed to him, because she was separated by li'an and her waiting period ended with the delivery of the first, and her second pregnancy occurred after the end of the waiting period, without marriage, so it did not need to be denied. He also said in al-Mughni: If one of the twins dies, he may perform li'an to negate their lineage. This is the view of al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah said: He is bound by the lineage of the living one, and he may perform li'an only to negate the hadd (prescribed punishment), because the dead cannot validly be negated by li'an, since his lineage has been cut off by his death, so there is no need to negate it by li'an, just as if his wife died, he would not perform li'an against her after her death, since the marriage has ended. And if the dead one is not negated, the living one is not negated either, because they are a single pregnancy. Our view is that the dead one is attributed to him, it is said "the son of so-and-so," he is obligated to prepare and shroud him, so he has the right to negate his lineage and drop his financial responsibility, like the living one, and as if the deceased had a child. End of the words of the author of al-Mughni.

The compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: The more apparent view is that if the dead child whose negation is desired has a child of his own, his ruling in li'an is like the ruling for the living, because his living child cannot be negated except by negating his father. So he may perform li'an to negate the lineage of the dead so that his child is cleared from him. This holds if we say that he may perform li'an after this long period, because he did not negate the dead child except after he had lived a lifetime in which he could have fathered children, and he may have been excused by absence for a long time. Likewise according to those who say that silence does not absolutely forfeit li'an, as was mentioned earlier. Likewise, if the intent is to obligate him to shroud and prepare the dead child, the more apparent view is that he may negate him by li'an in order to be free of the burden of his preparation and shrouding. And it is apparent that if he negates a child after its death, then if its mother is alive, li'an is necessary, because he is accusing his mother; and if the mother is dead, it follows the disagreement regarding the hadd of one who slanders a dead woman. On the view that there is a hadd, he may perform li'an; on the view that there is none, there is no li'an. We have already presented the disagreement on this. What we have mentioned is reinforced by what was mentioned shortly before, that he may perform li'an to negate a child, because two grounds for li'an combine: dropping the hadd and negating the child. From this you know that the more apparent view is not to consider whether the dead child left property or not. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Caution.

Know that the scholars disagreed about the twins of a woman subjected to li'an, whose negation was made by li'an: do they inherit from each other as full siblings (shaqiqan), or as siblings by the mother alone? Ibn al-Hajib of the Malikis said: They are full siblings. Khalil in al-Tawdih, his commentary on Ibn al-Hajib's abridgment in Maliki jurisprudence, said: That they are full siblings is the well-known position of Malik's school. al-Mughirah of the Malikis said: They inherit as siblings by the mother, like the well-known view among the Malikis regarding the twins of a fornicating woman and a woman raped.

The compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: What appears to us is that the twins of the woman subjected to li'an inherit from each other as siblings by the mother, and they are not ruled as full siblings, because they are not attached to a known father. And when they have no known father, there is no basis for their being full siblings. This is clarified by the fact that they are only attributed to their mother. From this you know that the well-known position of Malik in this issue is contrary to the more apparent view. As for the statement of Ibn Nafi' of the Malikis that the twins of a fornicating woman are full siblings, it contradicts scrupulous verification, because lineage is not attached to an adulterer so that he would be a father to his son from fornication. The narration from Ibn al-Qasim similar to Ibn Nafi's view, its apparent meaning is invalidity, as you see. As for what Ibn Rushd said in al-Bayan, that the twins of a captive woman and of a woman under safe-conduct are full siblings, its reasoning is clear. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The fifteenth issue: Know that if he marries her and then slanders her after the marriage, saying she committed fornication before he married her, the scholars disagreed: is he entitled to perform li'an against her, considering that the slander occurred while she was his wife, or is he given the hadd for slandering her and not allowed li'an, considering that at the time of the fornication he accused her of, she was a stranger to him and not a wife.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: If he slanders her after her marriage with fornication, attributing it to the time before the marriage, he is given the hadd and not li'an, whether or not there is a child. This is the view of Malik and Abu Thawr. It is narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Sha'bi. Al-Hasan, Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa, and the companions of opinion said: He may perform li'an, because he slandered his wife, so he falls under the general wording of Allah's statement: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [24:6], and because he slandered his wife, so it resembles the case where he slandered her without attributing it to before the marriage. Al-Sharif Abu Ja'far related another narration from Ahmad to the same effect. Al-Shafi'i said: If there is no child between them, he does not perform li'an; if there is a child, there are two opinions. Our argument is that he slandered her with a slander attributed to a state of separation, so it resembles the case where he slandered her while she was already divorced irrevocably. It differs from slandering a wife, because he needs it, since she angered him and betrayed him. And if there is a child between them, he needs to negate it. Here, if he married her while knowing of her fornication, then he is the one who was negligent in marrying a woman pregnant from fornication, so no way is legislated for him to negate it. End of al-Mughni.

The compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: The most apparent of the views in my opinion on this issue is that if there is no child, the husband is not allowed li'an, and he is given the hadd for slandering her unless he brings four witnesses, because he slandered her while she was a stranger, so he falls under the general wording of Allah's statement: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses﴾ [24:4], because he is slandering a chaste woman who is not a wife, and a subsequent marriage does not change the ruling that was established before it, as you see. If there is a child there that would be attributed to him if he were silent, and he knows it is not from him, relying on some of the matters permitting the negation of a child that we mentioned earlier, that he may perform li'an to negate the child.

The summary: It appears to us that he has the right to li'an to negate the child, not to repel the hadd. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The sixteenth issue: Concerning the case where he says to his wife: "You are divorced thrice, O adulteress." It is said: he performs li'an; it is said: he does not perform li'an, because the slander occurred only after the separation by three divorces, according to the view that she is separated by them. This is the view of the majority of scholars, including the four Imams and their companions.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: Muhanna' narrated: I asked Ahmad about a man who said to his wife, "You are divorced, O adulteress, thrice." He said: He performs li'an. I said: They say he is given the hadd, and only one (divorce) falls on her. He said: Evil is what they say. This man performs li'an, because he slandered her before the ruling of her separation, so it resembles slandering a revocably divorced wife. End of his words. It has some basis in reasoning. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The seventeenth issue: Concerning the case where his wife bears a child and he disowns it, and the wife agrees with him that the child is from someone else. Then the wife is liable to the hadd for fornication.

The scholars disagreed: does the child's lineage get negated by the mutual agreement of the two without li'an, or is it not negated except by li'an? Both views are narrated from Malik, and most of his narrators say it is not negated except by li'an.

The compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: The more apparent of the two views in my opinion is that it is not negated from the husband except by his li'an, and his right to the child's lineage is not dropped by his wife's confirmation of the husband's claim, because the child has a right to the attribution of its lineage, so it is not dropped except by the husband's li'an. As for the wife, li'an is not valid from her in this case, because she is confirming the husband's claim.

* *

The eighteenth issue: Know that the more apparent view for us regarding a man who slanders his wife, and she demands the hadd for her slander, and he produces two witnesses to her confession of the fornication with which he slandered her, is that the ruling of this issue is based on the disagreement over whether confession of fornication is established by two witnesses like other confessions, or is not established except by four witnesses. Whoever says it is established by two witnesses must hold that the man is not given the hadd for slandering her, because her confession of fornication was established by the two witnesses. On the other view he is given the hadd, because her confession was not established. This is the more apparent view for us. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

The Nineteenth Issue: Know that the more apparent view is that if the two witnesses testify against him that he slandered his wife, while he has also slandered them (I mean the two witnesses), their testimony regarding the slander of the woman is not accepted. This is because, when they claimed that he had slandered them, they became his enemies, since slander necessitates enmity. Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: If two witnesses testify that he slandered so-and-so, and he slandered us, their testimony is not accepted, because they have acknowledged his enmity toward them, and the testimony of an enemy is not accepted against his enemy. If, however, he absolved him and the enmity ended, and then they testified against him with that same slander, it is not accepted, because it was rejected due to suspicion, so it is not accepted thereafter, like the wrongdoer (fasiq) whose testimony is rejected due to his wrongdoing, and then he repents and it is restored. If they had claimed against him that he slandered them, then he absolved him and the enmity ended, and then they testified against him regarding the slander of his wife, their testimony is accepted, because they were not rejected in this testimony. If they testified that he slandered his wife, and then after that claimed that he slandered them, then if they attributed their claim to a time before their testimony, their testimony is invalidated, since they acknowledged that he was their enemy when they testified against him. If they did not attribute it to that time, and that was before the judgment based on their testimony, judgment is not given on it, because judgment is not given against him on the testimony of two enemies. If it was after the judgment, it is not invalidated, because the judgment was completed before the occurrence of the impediment, such as the manifestation of wrongdoing. If they testified that he slandered his wife and his mother, their testimony is not accepted, because it was rejected in part due to suspicion, so it must be rejected entirely. If they testified against their father that he slandered the co-wife of their mother, their testimony is accepted, and this is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah and al-Shafi'i in his later view (al-jadid). In his earlier view (al-qadim) he said: it is not accepted, because they bring to their mother a benefit, namely that he will perform li'an with her, so she will be separated and it will benefit their mother. This is not correct, because his li'an with her is based on his knowledge of her adultery, not on a testimony against him about what he does not acknowledge. If they testified to the divorce of the co-wife, there are two opinions: the first is that it is not accepted, because they bring to their mother a benefit, namely its advantage to their mother. The second is that it is accepted, because they do not bring a benefit to themselves. End of quotation from al-Mughni. The author (the compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him) says: all of this has no explicit text, and some of it is not free from disagreement. The more apparent view is the non-acceptance of their testimony regarding the divorce of their mother's co-wife, because they are suspected of bringing a benefit to their mother, since the divorce of the co-wife contains a benefit for her co-wife, as is well known, and a person's testimony regarding what benefits his mother is not free from suspicion, as you see. And Allah knows best.

* *

The Twentieth Issue: concerning the difference of languages or times in the slander or the acknowledgment of it.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: If one witness testifies that he acknowledged in Arabic that he slandered her, and another testifies that he acknowledged that in non-Arabic (ajamiyyah), the testimony is complete, because the difference between Arabic and non-Arabic relates to the acknowledgment and not to the slander, and it is possible that the slander is one and the acknowledgment of it occurred on two occasions. Likewise, if one of them testifies that he acknowledged on Thursday that he slandered her, and another testifies that he acknowledged that on Friday, the testimony is complete for the reason we mentioned. If one of them testifies that he slandered her in Arabic and the other testifies that he slandered her in non-Arabic, or one testifies that he acknowledged that he slandered her in Arabic or non-Arabic, or one testifies that he acknowledged that he slandered her in Arabic, or on Thursday, and the other testifies that he acknowledged that he slandered her in non-Arabic, or on Friday, or one on Thursday, and the other testifies that he slandered her on Friday, there are two opinions:
The first: the testimony is complete, and this is the view of Abu Bakr and the position of Abu Hanifah, because mention of the time is not a condition of the testimony, and likewise the language, so the difference has no effect, just as if one of them testified that he acknowledged slandering her on Thursday in Arabic, and the other testified that he acknowledged slandering her on Friday in non-Arabic. The second: the testimony is not complete, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i, because they are two slanders, and the testimony is not complete regarding either of them, so it is not established, just as if one of them testified that he married her on Thursday and the other testified that he married her on Friday. The acknowledgment of slander differs, for it is possible that the one who acknowledges it is one person who acknowledged it at two times in two languages. End of quotation from al-Mughni.

The author (the compiler, may Allah pardon him and forgive him) says: This issue is the well-known one among scholars concerning whether testimony is combined (tulaffaq) regarding acts and statements or not. Some scholars say it is combined regarding statements but not acts, and some say it is combined regarding both. The distinction between them is not clear, and their statement that "they are two slanders, and the testimony is not complete regarding either of them" may be said about it too. Likewise, an acknowledgment whose time or language differs is two acknowledgments, and the testimony is not complete regarding either of them. This issue has no explicit text, and each of the views concerning it has a basis in reasoning. The disagreement mentioned and the absence of a text may well be a doubt that averts the prescribed penalty (hadd). And Allah knows best.

* *

The Twenty-First Issue: Know that what appears to us to be correct is that whoever denies that his wife's pregnancy is his by li'an, the child is disowned from him, and he is not obliged to perform another li'an after its birth. This is the verification, if Allah wills, and by it you know that the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, and whoever agreed with him among the people of Kufa, and the view of al-Khiraqi and whoever agreed with him among the Hanbalis, that the pregnancy cannot validly be disowned by li'an, so li'an must be after birth, because the pregnancy before birth is not certain, given the possibility that it is wind, is contrary to the verification as it appears to us regarding the disowning of the pregnancy by li'an. This is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i and whoever agreed with them from the people of the Hijaz, as Ibn Qudamah transmitted it from them in al-Mughni. The story of Hilal ibn Umayyah, may Allah be pleased with him, is explicit that the Prophet ﷺ disowned the pregnancy of his wife by li'an and did not oblige him to repeat the li'an after birth. The narration that gives the impression that his li'an was after birth, we have clarified the answer to it earlier, with what Ibn Hajar answered in al-Fath. And Allah knows best.

* *

The Twenty-Second Issue: concerning the ruling on one who slanders his wife with sodomy (liwat). We clarified in Surah Hud, in the discussion of the story of the people of Lut, the views of scholars on the punishment of the sodomite, and we showed that the strongest of them in evidence is the killing of the doer and the one to whom it is done. Accordingly, there is no hadd for slander with sodomy; rather, there is only ta'zir (discretionary punishment) in it. We mentioned the view of those scholars who said that the ruling on sodomy is the ruling on adultery, and according to this view the one who slanders with sodomy performs li'an, and if he refuses li'an, he is punished with hadd. And Allah knows best.

* *

The Twenty-Third Issue: concerning the ruling on one whose wife bears a child that cannot possibly be his. The child is not attributed to him, and there is no need to disown it by li'an, because it is known that it is not his, as if he married a woman and she brought forth a complete child in less than six months, since the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, as we clarified in Surah al-Ra'd. There is no disagreement among scholars on this, and likewise if the husband is a boy who cannot usually father a child because of his youth and the like.

Know that what appears to us to be correct is that every child borne by the wife of a minor before his puberty is not attributed to him, and no li'an is needed. By this you know that the view of those Hanbalis and whoever agreed with them, who said that if the husband is ten years old the child is attributed to him, and likewise at nine and a half years, as the judge among the Hanbalis said, is contrary to the verification. Their evidence for attributing the child to a husband who is ten years old, based on the hadith: "Command them to pray at ten, and separate them in their beds," is clearly invalid, even though Ibn Qudamah relied on it, with his knowledge, as did others among the Hanbalis.

So the verification, if Allah wills, is what Abu Bakr among the Hanbalis said: that the child is not attributed to him until he reaches puberty. This is clear and obvious. Likewise, if a man married a woman in a session and divorced her in it before he left them, then his wife brought forth a child six months from the time of the contract, or a man from the East married a woman from the West, or vice versa, and six months passed and she brought forth a child, the child is not attributed to him. Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: Malik and al-Shafi'i said this, and Abu Hanifah said: his lineage is attributed to him, because the child is attributed to him by the contract and the period of pregnancy; do you not see that you say, when the period of possibility has passed, the child is attributed, even if it is known that intercourse did not occur from him? End of quotation.

The author (the compiler, may Allah pardon him and forgive him) says: The verification, if Allah wills, is the non-attribution of the child in the cases mentioned, since it is known that it is not his, and there is no need to disown it. And Allah knows best.

* *

The Twenty-Fourth Issue: Know that the strongest of the views and the strongest in evidence is that the spouses in li'an are permanently forbidden to each other, so they never reunite. Hadiths have come to this effect, among them what Abu Dawud related from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, in which: "Then the sunnah continued regarding the two who perform li'an, that they be separated, and then they never reunite." End of quotation.

In Nayl al-Awtar, concerning this hadith, it says: Abu Dawud and al-Mundhiri were silent about it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. Among them is what al-Daraqutni related from Sahl also, in which: "So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them and said: 'They shall never reunite.'" End of quotation through the transmission of al-Majd in al-Muntaqa. The author of Nayl al-Awtar said concerning it: In its chain is Iyad ibn Abd Allah; in al-Taqrib it says: "In him there is some weakness, but Muslim has nevertheless related from him." End of quotation.

Among them is what al-Daraqutni related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Those who perform li'an, when they separate, shall never reunite." End of quotation, through the transmission of al-Majd also.

Among them is what al-Daraqutni also related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The sunnah has continued regarding the two who perform li'an that they shall never reunite." And what al-Daraqutni also related from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, who both said: "The sunnah has continued that the two who perform li'an shall not reunite." The author of Nayl al-Awtar said concerning the hadith of Ibn Abbas: Abu Dawud related something similar in a long story, and in its chain is Abbad ibn Mansur, concerning whom there is criticism. He said concerning the hadith of Ali and Ibn Mas'ud: Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Shaybah also related them both. End of quotation.

By this you know that the permanence of the prohibition is more correct than the view of those scholars who said that if he retracts his accusation he is punished with hadd, and her prohibition upon him is not permanent, and he becomes a suitor like other suitors. This is related from Abu Hanifah, Muhammad, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah. The more apparent view is that if he retracts his accusation, the child is attributed to him and he is punished with hadd, in contrast to Ata', who said that he is not punished with hadd.

Note.
Know that the views of scholars on the separation by li'an we have already presented in full in Surah al-Baqarah, in our lengthy discussion of the verse: "Divorce is twice" (al-Baqarah 2:229). We have also already presented the words of scholars and their disagreement regarding the li'an of the mute in Surah Maryam. Let us suffice with what we have mentioned of the rulings connected with this verse. Whoever wishes to exhaust the issues of li'an should consult the books of the furu' (positive law) of the four madhhabs.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 21:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure, but Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

In this verse, He—glorified and exalted—makes clear that were it not for His grace and His mercy, none of His creation would have been purified; but by His grace and His mercy, He purifies whom He wills of His creatures.

It is understood from the verse that He does not enable anyone to purify himself under any circumstances. This meaning contained in this noble verse is also expressed elsewhere, such as His statement, may He be exalted: (p-485) ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa': 49], and His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who has feared Him﴾ [an-Najm: 32].

The purification (zakah) in this verse means cleansing from the impurities of polytheism and sins.

As for His statement ﴿but Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ [an-Nur: 21], it means: He cleanses him from the filth of disbelief and sins through His enabling and guidance to faith, sincere repentance, and righteous deeds.

What these verses indicate is not contradicted by His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [ash-Shams: 9], nor by His statement: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14], on the view that the meaning of tazakka is "cleansed himself from the filth of disbelief and sins," not that what is meant by them is specifically the zakat al-fitr (obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan). The reason for this in His statement "who purifies it" is that one does not purify it except by Allah's enabling and His guidance to it toward righteous action, and His acceptance of it from him.

The matter is likewise in His statement: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾, as is not hidden.

The more apparent view is that His statement ﴿what purified any one of you ever﴾ [an-Nur: 21], etc., is the answer (jawab) to the "lawla" (were it not) that precedes it, contrary to those who claimed that it is the answer to the "lawla" in His statement ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾ [an-Nur: 20], etc. The omission of the answer to "lawla" has occurred repeatedly in the verses before this verse, due to the indication of the contextual clues upon it,

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 22 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

This noble verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. Mistah, the aforementioned, was among the emigrants and was poor, and his mother was the daughter of Abu Bakr's maternal aunt. Abu Bakr used to spend on him because of his poverty, his kinship, and his emigration. He was among those who spoke against the Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) with the slander mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you﴾ [al-Nur: 11], which is that they accused her of committing adultery with Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami (may Allah be pleased with him).

The story of the slander (qissat al-ifk) is well known and established in ten verses of this noble surah and in the authentic hadiths. When 'A'ishah's innocence was declared in the mentioned verses, Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on Mistah and would not benefit him with any benefit, after he had slandered 'A'ishah falsely and unjustly. So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah﴾, and so on.

His saying: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear﴾ means: let them not swear. The word ya'tali is of the form yaf'ali from al-ali'yah (al-alīyah), which is the oath. The Arabs say: "alā yu'lī" and "ā'talā ya'talī" when one swears. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for those who swear off their wives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 226], meaning: those who swear; it is the imperfect of "alā yu'lī" when one swears. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Once, on the back of the dune, she made me wait, and she swore an oath that would not be undone.

That is, she swore an oath. And the saying of 'Atikah bint Zayd al-'Adawiyyah, lamenting her husband 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them):

So I swore that my eye would not cease to be sorrowful over you, and my skin would not cease to be dust-colored.

Al-alīyah is the oath. From this is the saying of another, praising 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz:

Few are his oaths, and he guards his oath; and even if an oath slips from him, he fulfills it.

That is: the people of virtue and wealth, that is, richness, like Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), do not swear that they will not give to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah, like Mistah ibn Uthathah. His saying "an yu'tū" means: they should not swear against giving, or they should not swear that they will not give. The deletion of the preposition before the verbal noun formed from "an" and its clause is regular. Likewise, the deletion of the negative "lā" before the imperfect after an oath is also established, and the fact that the oath here is forbidden does not affect this. The second object of "yu'tū" is omitted, meaning: that they give the near of kin the provision and kindness, as Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) did.

Some scholars said: His saying "wa lā ya'tali" means: the people of virtue and wealth should not fall short, like Abu Bakr, in giving to the near of kin like Mistah. According to this, "ya'tali" is of the form yaf'ali from "lā ya'lū fi al-amr," when one falls short in it and delays.

From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves; they will not spare you corruption﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118] (p-487), meaning: they do not fall short in harming you. From this, with this meaning, is the saying of al-Ja'di:

And a grey-haired, bare man who binds his waistband, who is blamed for his striving in battle, and he did not fall short.

And the saying of another:

Indeed my sons are women of truth; so they did not fall short of their father, nor did they do wrong.

His saying "fa-mā ālā banī" means: they did not fall short, nor delay. The first meaning is the more correct, because Abu Bakr's oath that he would not benefit Mistah with any benefit, and the revelation of the noble verse concerning that oath, is well known. What this noble verse contains of prohibition against swearing off doing good, such as giving to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants, has also come in other places, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make reconciliation among people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 224], meaning: do not swear by Allah against doing good. So when it is said to you: "Fear Allah and be righteous and make reconciliation among people," you say: "We have sworn by Allah that we will not do that," and thus you make the oath by Allah a cause for refraining from doing good. This is the more correct interpretation of the verse.

We have already mentioned the indication of these two verses for the meaning stated, and we mentioned what clarifies it from the authentic hadiths in surah al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for ineffective oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have intended in oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89].

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾ contains a command from Allah to the believers: when some of their Muslim brothers wrong them, they should pardon their wrong and overlook it. The origin of "al-'afw" is from "'afat al-rih al-athar," when the wind effaces a trace, meaning: they should efface the traces of the offense by their forbearance and forgiveness. As for al-safh (overlooking), some scholars said it is derived from "safhat al-'unuq" (the side of the neck), meaning: turn away from repaying their offense, as if you turn it aside with the side of the neck, turning away from it. What this noble verse contains of pardon and overlooking is explained in other places, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous, who spend in ease and in hardship, who restrain anger and pardon people; and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133-134]. This verse shows that restraining anger and pardoning people are among the attributes of the people of Paradise, and that suffices as an exhortation to it. It also shows that this is among the good deeds that Allah loves those who possess. And like His saying, the Exalted (p-488): ﴿If you show good or conceal it or pardon an evil, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾ [al-Nisa': 149]. In this verse He has shown that pardon while having the power to punish is among His attributes, the Exalted, and that suffices as an exhortation to it. And like His saying: ﴿So pardon with gracious pardon﴾ [al-Hijr: 85], and His saying: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43], and other verses.

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ is evidence that pardon and overlooking an offending Muslim are among the causes of forgiveness of sins, and the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. For this reason, when it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "Yes, by Allah, we love that our Lord should forgive us," and he returned to spending on Mistah. The object of "an yaghfira Allah" is omitted because it is known: that is, He forgives you your sins.

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Ulī al-qurbā﴾ means: the people of kinship. The word ulā is a plural noun that has no singular from its own form, and it is inflected like the sound masculine plural.

* *

Benefit

In this noble verse there is evidence that major sins do not nullify righteous deeds, because Mistah ibn Uthathah's emigration was from his righteous deeds, and his slander of 'A'ishah was among the major sins, yet it did not nullify his emigration; for Allah said of him after his slander of her: ﴿and the emigrants in the way of Allah﴾. This shows that his emigration in the way of Allah was not nullified by his slander of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her).

Al-Qurtubi said: In this verse there is evidence that slander, even if it is a major sin, does not nullify deeds, because Allah described Mistah after His saying with emigration and faith, and likewise all major sins; and nothing nullifies deeds except associating partners with Allah. Allah said: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. End.

What was mentioned, that the verse describes Mistah with faith, does not appear from the verse, although it is known.

Al-Qurtubi also said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: this is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah. Then he said after this: some scholars said: this is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, in terms of Allah's kindness to the slanderers who are sinners by this wording. It was also said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47]. Allah the Exalted has also said in another verse: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, in gardens of delight, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22] (p-489), so He explained the great bounty in this verse and gave good tidings of it to the believers in that one.

Among the verses of hope is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [al-Zumar: 53], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. Some said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5], because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not be pleased with anyone of his community remaining in the Fire. End of al-Qurtubi's words.

Some scholars said: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the verse of debt: it is the longest verse in the Glorious Qur'an, and in it Allah, Blessed and Exalted, clarified the means sufficient to safeguard debt from being lost. Even if the debt is small, as His saying in it indicates: ﴿and do not be weary of writing it, whether small or large, for its term﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. They said: this is from the care in the verse of debt for preserving the wealth of the Muslim and not letting it be lost, even a little, and it indicates the complete concern for the interests of the Muslim. This shows that the Subtle, the All-Aware, will not lose it on the Day of Resurrection when the terror intensifies and his need for his Lord is severe.

The one who restricts it, may Allah pardon and forgive him, says: Among the most hopeful verses of the Glorious Qur'an is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants; but among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty. Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk. And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative, who has settled us in the home of settlement from His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, and no weariness touches us therein"﴾ [Fatir: 32-35].

In this noble verse Allah has shown that the inheritance of this Book by this Ummah is evidence that Allah has chosen it, in His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾, and He explained that they are three categories:

The first: the one who wrongs himself, who obeys Allah but also disobeys Him. This is the one about whom Allah said: ﴿They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad; perhaps Allah will accept their repentance﴾ [al-Tawbah: 102].

(p-490) The second: the moderate one, who obeys Allah and does not disobey Him, but does not draw near to Him with voluntary acts of obedience.

The third category: the foremost in good deeds (al-sābiq bil-khayrāt), who performs the obligatory duties, avoids the prohibited acts, and draws near to Allah through acts of obedience and voluntary devotions that are not obligatory. This is, according to the most correct of the opinions, the interpretation of "one who wrongs himself," "the moderate one," and "the foremost." Then He, exalted is He, made clear that their inheritance of the Book is a great favor from Him upon them. Then He promised all of them the Gardens of Eden, and He does not break His promise, in His saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden, they will enter them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and no weariness will touch us therein﴾. The waw in "yadkhulūnahā" ("they will enter them") includes the one who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the foremost, in verification. Therefore some of the scholars said: this waw deserves to be written with the ink of the eyes. His true promise of the Gardens of Eden to all the categories of this Ummah, and the first of them being the one who wrongs himself, indicates that this verse is among the most hopeful verses of the Qur'an. No Muslim remains outside the three categories, so the true promise of Paradise in the verse includes all Muslims. For this reason He said after it, connected to it: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, the fire of Hell is theirs. It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾, up to His saying: ﴿So there is not for the wrongdoers any helper﴾ [Fāṭir: 36–37].

The scholars differed regarding the reason for placing the one who wrongs himself before the moderate and the foremost in the promise of Paradise. Some of them said: He placed the wrongdoer first so that he would not despair, and delayed the foremost in good so that he would not be amazed by his deed and thus be nullified. Others said: He placed the wrongdoer first because most of the people of Paradise are those who wrong themselves, since those who never committed a sin are fewer than others, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿except those who believed and did righteous deeds, and few are they﴾ [Ṣād: 24].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾. In this noble verse, He, exalted and most high, mentioned that those who accuse chaste, heedless, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and that for them there is a great punishment, on the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet bear witness against them concerning what they used to do. And He made clear in another place that some parts of the disbelievers other than the tongue will bear witness against them on the Day of Resurrection, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Day We shall seal upon their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight and their skins will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾. ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why do you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has given us speech, Who gives speech to all things."﴾ (p. 491) up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves, lest your hearing and your sight and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do. And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers﴾ [Fussilat: 20–23].

The Exalted's saying: ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their full due, the truth﴾. The meaning of "dīn" (here, "due" or requital) in this verse is recompense (al-jazā'). This is shown by His saying "yuwaffīhim" (He will pay them in full), because "tawfiyah" (payment in full) indicates recompense,

• like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾ [al-Najm: 41],

• and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 185],

• and His saying: ﴿Every soul will be paid in full what it has earned﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 161],

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying "dīnahum" (their due), it means their recompense, which is in the utmost justice and fairness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "dīnahum al-ḥaqq" means their due recompense, which is what they are owed and deserve. The first (interpretation) is more correct, because Allah recompenses His servants with complete fairness and perfect justice. There are many Qur'anic verses on this,

• like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed He doubles it﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 40],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾ [Yūnus: 44],

• and His saying: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 47], and other verses besides these, as their explanation has already passed. And among the Qur'anic uses of "dīn" in the sense of recompense is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Fātiḥah: 4].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. That is better for you, that you may remember.﴾

Know that this noble verse has been difficult for many scholars, because it uses the word *istinas* (seeking intimacy, or being at ease) to express *istidhan* (seeking permission), even though the two words differ in root and meaning.

Ibn Hajar said in *Fath al-Bari*: Al-Tahawi reported that *al-istinas* in the dialect of Yemen means *al-istidhan* (seeking permission). There are two interpretations of this noble verse that fit its wording, and each has a witness from the Book of Allah, the Exalted.

The first interpretation: *istinas* here is from the apparent sense of being at ease, which is the opposite of feeling estranged. The one who knocks at another's door does not know whether he will be permitted to enter or not, so he is like one who feels estranged because the situation is hidden from him. When he is given permission, he becomes at ease and his estrangement goes away. Since being at ease is necessarily connected to permission, the necessary concept (being at ease) is named while the thing it necessarily entails (permission) is intended. Naming the necessary concept while meaning what it entails is a well-known Arabic style. Those who hold that the Qur'an contains metaphor say that this is *majaz mursal* (a loose metonymy). According to this view, when the necessary concept *istinas* is used in the verse while its entailed meaning *idhn* (permission) is intended, the meaning becomes: "until you seek permission." The Exalted's saying supports this meaning: ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], and His saying after it: ﴿So do not enter them until permission is given to you﴾ [al-Nur: 28]. Al-Zamakhshari, after mentioning this interpretation, said: "This is of the category of *kinaya* (allusion) and *irdaf* (implication), because this kind of being at ease follows permission, so it was placed in the position of permission."

The second interpretation of the verse: *istinas* means seeking information and uncovering the situation. It is an *istif'al* form from *anasa al-shay'* when one perceives the thing clearly and openly, or knows it.

The meaning: "until you seek out and uncover the situation, whether you are permitted or not." The Arabs say: *Istanis hal tara ahadan* ("Look and see whether you see anyone"), and *istanasttu fa lam ara ahadan* ("I looked and saw no one"), meaning: I found out and learned. Of this meaning is the Exalted's saying: ﴿If you perceive in them maturity of judgment, then deliver to them their property﴾ [al-Nisa': 6], meaning: if you know their maturity and it becomes clear to you. And the Exalted's saying about Musa: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring you from it a burning brand﴾ [Ta-Ha: 10], and His saying: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he perceived from the side of the mount a fire﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]. So the meaning of *anasa naran* ("he perceived a fire") is that he saw it clearly and openly. Of this meaning is the saying of Al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani:

"As if my saddle, when the day had passed away with us at Dhi al-Jalil, was upon a wild donkey that is at ease, one alone,
From the wild asses of Wajra, speckled in its legs, lean in its flank, like the sword of the polisher, keen."

His saying "upon one that is at ease" means a wild ass, to which he likened his she-camel. Its being "at ease" means that it uncovers and perceives (the situation): it senses the hunters by their scent and the keenness of its sight as it looks at them. Also from this is the saying of al-Harith ibn Hilliza al-Yashkuri describing an ostrich, to which he likened his she-camel:

"She perceived a sound, and the spears frightened her at the time of afternoon, when evening had drawn near."

His saying "she perceived a sound" means she sensed a faint voice. This interpretation, that the meaning of *tasta'nisu* is "you uncover and find out whether you are permitted," is, in my view, more apparent, though some scholars have preferred the first interpretation. There is a third interpretation of the verse, which we have left aside because it does not appeal to us.

From what we have mentioned, you know that what is reported from Ibn Abbas and others, that the original text of the verse was "until you seek permission" (*hatta tasta'dhinu*) and that the scribes erred in writing, writing *tasta'nisu* by mistake in place of *tasta'dhinu*, is not to be relied upon. It is impossible that this be authentically reported from Ibn Abbas, even if some scholars have declared its chain sound. Even if we assume its authenticity, it would be among the recitations that were abrogated (*naskh*, the cancellation of a ruling or recitation) and abandoned, and the one who recited it may not have known of that.
