We have learned from what we have mentioned, in the narrations of the hadith of Ibn Umar that is agreed upon, that in some of its agreed-upon narrations the command to men to grant women permission to go out to the mosque is restricted to the night, while in others it is unrestricted and not limited to the night, and this is the majority of narrations, as Ibn Hajar indicated in al-Fath.

It may occur to the reader that husbands are only commanded to grant women permission specifically at night, because it is more concealing, and this is strengthened in his mind by the principle established in the usul al-fiqh of applying the unrestricted to the restricted. So the unrestricted narrations are read as restricted to the night, and the mentioned permission is therefore specific to the night.

Al-Shinqiti said: The more evident view to me is to give precedence to the unrestricted narrations, not limited to the night, because of the abundance of authentic hadiths indicating that women attended the prayer with him (ﷺ) at times other than night, such as the agreed-upon hadith of Aisha mentioned above, indicating their attendance with him (ﷺ) at Subh, which is a daytime prayer, not a night prayer. It does not take the ruling of the night prayer, given that they return to their homes unrecognised because of the darkness, since that time is certainly part of the day, not the night. That it belongs to the day prevents restriction to the night. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

As for what is stipulated for the permissibility of women going out to the mosques, it is:

* *

Fourth issue:

Know that the going out of a woman to the mosque is subject, according to the scholars, to conditions all of which return to one thing: that at the time of her going out to the mosque, the woman is not wearing anything that invites temptation, together with safety from corruption.

Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim, regarding the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah," the following text: This and similar hadiths of the chapter clearly show that they may not be prevented from the mosque, but with conditions the scholars mentioned, derived from the hadiths: that she not be wearing perfume, not be adorned, not have anklets whose sound is heard, not wear luxurious clothing, not mix with men, and not be a young woman or similar to one who might be tempted, and that there be nothing on the road that causes fear of corruption or the like. End of the relevant point of al-Nawawi's words.

Al-Shinqiti said: These conditions mentioned by al-Nawawi and others: some of them are established from the Prophet (ﷺ), and some have no explicit text but are attached to the texts because they share its reason. Applying some of them by analogy is not free from objection, as you will see the full explanation of all this, God willing. As for what is established from him (ﷺ) of those conditions, it is the absence of perfume: the condition for a woman's permissibility to go out to the mosque is that she not be wearing perfume.

Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his Sahih: Marwan ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Makhramah informed me, from his father, from Busr ibn Sa'id, that Zaynab al-Thaqafiyyah used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "If one of you women attends the Isha prayer, let her not use perfume that night."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who narrated to me Bukayr ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashajj, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Zaynab, the wife of Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'If one of you women attends the mosque, let her not touch perfume.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Yahya said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah informed us, from Yazid ibn Khusayfah, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Any woman who has touched incense, let her not attend the late evening prayer with us." End of quote.

This authentic hadith, which Muslim included in his Sahih from two Companions, Abu Hurayrah and Zaynab, the wife of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with all of them), is explicit that a woman who uses perfume may not go out to the mosque. This is supported by what Abu Dawud related in his Sunan: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah, but let them go out while they are tafilat (unperfumed)." End of quote. His words "wa hunna tafilat" mean: not wearing perfume. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on al-Muhadhdhab, regarding this hadith: Abu Dawud narrated it with a sound chain according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim. "Tafilat" is with an opening fatha on the ta' and a kasra on the fa', meaning those who abandon perfume. End of quote. From this is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

**Part 3 of 3**

؎إذا ما الضَّجِيعُ ابْتَزَّها مِن ثِيابِها ∗∗∗ تَمِيلُ عَلَيْهِ هَوْنَةَ غَيْرِ مِتْفالِي
("When her bedfellow strips her of her garments, she inclines toward him gently, not one who is lax.")

This hadith was also related by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Khuzaymah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Ibn Hibban related it from the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid. So said al-Shawkani and others.

Now that you know these hadiths indicate that a woman who wears perfume is not permitted to go out to the masjid, because she stirs the desire of men by the scent of her perfume.

Know that the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) extended to perfume what has the same meaning, such as visible adornment, the sound of the khalkhal (anklet), luxurious clothing, mixing with men, and similar things, on the common ground that all of these are causes of fitnah (temptation) by stirring the desire of men. Its basis is clear, as you see. The Shafi'is extended this ruling to a young woman in general, because a young man is a source of fitnah. They restricted going out to the masajid to elderly women. The more apparent view is that when a young woman goes out modestly covered, not wearing perfume, and not clothed in any other cause of fitnah, she is permitted to go out to the masjid, due to the generality of the texts mentioned earlier. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

(p-547) The fifth issue: Know that the prayer of women in their houses is better for them than prayer in the masajid, even if the masjid is the Masjid of the Prophet (ﷺ). From this you know that his saying (ﷺ): "A prayer in this my masjid is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Sacred Masjid" is specific to men. As for women, their prayer in their houses is better for them than prayer in congregation in the masjid.

Abu Dawud said in his Sunan: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Yazid ibn Harun related to us, al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, Habib ibn Abi Thabit related to me, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prevent your women from the masajid, but their houses are better for them."

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab regarding this hadith: The hadith of Ibn 'Umar is sahih; Abu Dawud related it with this wording, with a sahih chain according to the condition of al-Bukhari, end of quote.

This hadith was also related by Imam Ahmad. Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: Something has come in some narrations of this hadith and others indicating that a woman's prayer in her house is better than her prayer in the masjid. This is in the narration of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ibn 'Umar, with the wording: "Do not prevent your women from the masajid, but their houses are better for them." Abu Dawud related it, and Ibn Khuzaymah graded it sahih. Ahmad and al-Tabarani have, from the hadith of Umm Humayd al-Sa'idiyyah, that she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love to pray with you." He said: "I know. Your prayer in your house is better for you than your prayer in your chamber, your prayer in your chamber is better than your prayer in your courtyard, your prayer in your courtyard is better than your prayer in the masjid of your people, and your prayer in the masjid of your people is better than your prayer in the masjid of the congregation." The chain of Ahmad is hasan, and it has a supporting report from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in Abu Dawud. The reason that praying in seclusion is better for her is the certainty of safety from fitnah therein. End of the relevant part of Ibn Hajar's words.

As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud to which he referred, it is what Abu Dawud related in his Sunan: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us that 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to them, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Muwarriq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman's prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her chamber, and her prayer in her inner room is better than her prayer in her house." End quote.

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab regarding this hadith: Abu Dawud related it with a sahih chain according to the condition of Muslim. Ahmad related from Umm Salamah, from him (ﷺ): "The best of the masajid of women is the innermost part of their houses."

(p-548) From the texts we have mentioned, you know that the prayer of women in their houses is better for them than their prayer in congregation in the Masjid of the Prophet (ﷺ) or other masajid, because this is established from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Among what confirms their praying in their houses is what they have innovated of entering the masjid in short clothing, which is a cause of fitnah, and crowding men at the doors of the masjid when entering and leaving. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related in their Sahihayn from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen what the women have done, he would have prevented them from the masjid, just as the Children of Israel prevented their women."

From what we have mentioned of the hadiths, you know that the implied contrary meaning (mafhum al-mukhalafah) in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glorifying Him therein morning and evening are men﴾ and so on, is valid, and that it is not mafhum al-laqab (the implication of a proper name). We have clarified the mentioned implication by the Sunnah, as you have seen. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 37:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾. In this noble verse, Exalted and Majestic is He, mentions that the men who glorify Him in the mosques morning and evening, and the rest of their described attributes, are those who fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about. This is the Day of Resurrection, because of the severity of its terror. The great magnitude of the terror of that Day, and its effect upon hearts and eyes, which this noble verse indicates, is mentioned in many verses of the Mighty Book of Allah, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling; their eyes will be humbled﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 8-9], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking﴾ [Ghafir: 18], and similar verses indicating the greatness of that Day, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿How then will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will make children grey-haired? The sky will be split by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 17-18], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we do not desire from you reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing﴾ [al-Insan: 9-10], along with other verses. Regarding the meaning of the turning of hearts and eyes, the commentators have several opinions, which al-Qurtubi and others have mentioned.

The most evident of them in my view is that the turning of hearts is their movement from their places out of extreme fear, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿when hearts will be at the throats﴾. And that the turning of eyes is their roving and their circling in looking in all directions out of extreme fear, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one who has fainted from death﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19], and as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10]. So the circling and the swerving mentioned are the means by which the meaning of the turning of eyes is known, even though they are mentioned in the context of fear of what is disliked in this world.

The Words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty﴾.

Apparently, the lam in His words "That He may reward them" (liyajziyahum) is connected to His words "glorify" (yusabbihu), meaning: they glorify Him for Him, and they fear a Day, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did. As for His words in this noble verse, "and increase them from His bounty," apparently this increase from His bounty, Exalted is He, is the multiplication of good deeds, as indicated by His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof﴾ [al-An'am: 160], and His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [an-Nisa: 40], and His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

Some of the people of knowledge said: the increase here is like the increase in His words: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and an increase﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The more correct view is that "the best" (al-husna) is Paradise, and "the increase" (al-ziyadah) is looking upon the Noble Face of Allah. This is one of the two opinions regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35].

We have already mentioned the view of some of the people of knowledge that His words, Exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾, and similar verses, indicate that the permissible (al-mubah) is good, because His words "the best of what they did" are in the form of a superlative (sighat tafdil), and the superlative form mentioned indicates that among their deeds there is something good for which they were not rewarded, and it is the permissible. He said in Maraqi as-Su'ud:

"What our Lord did not forbid is good,
and what is other than it is ugly and reprehensible."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing.﴾ In this noble verse, exalted and most high is He, mentioned that the deeds of the disbelievers are null and void, and that they amount to nothing; for He said, regarding the mirage with which He likened them: ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing.﴾ What this noble verse indicates of the nullity of the deeds of the disbelievers (p-550) has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ [Ibrahim: 18], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23], in addition to other verses.

We have already presented that the deed of the disbeliever, if it is upon the correct manner, he is rewarded for it in this world, as we have clarified in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer﴾ [an-Nahl: 97].

Verses of the Book of Allah have indicated that the disbeliever benefits from his deed in this world, but not in the Hereafter, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [ash-Shura: 20], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein becomes void, and worthless is what they used to do﴾ [Hud: 15-16]. And this which these verses indicate of the disbeliever's benefit from his righteous deed in this world, but not in the Hereafter, is established in Sahih Muslim and others from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him); as we have clarified in the discussion of the aforementioned verse of an-Nahl. It is also one of the two interpretations of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He found Allah with him, so He paid him his account﴾ [an-Nur: 39], meaning: He paid him his account in this world according to this view. Allah, exalted and most high, has also made clear in Surat Bani Isra'il that what the verses indicate of the disbeliever's benefit from his righteous deed in this world is conditioned upon the will of Allah, exalted is He, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the fleeting [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish. Then We have made for him Hell; he will burn therein, blamed and banished﴾ [al-Isra': 18].

Warning (tanbih).

In this noble verse there is a well-known question, which we mentioned, and mentioned the answer to it, in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book), in our saying there: It is not hidden what comes to the mind of the pronoun in His saying "jaahu" (came to it) indicates a existing thing upon which the coming falls, because the occurrence of coming upon nothingness is not conceivable; and it is known that a relative attribute is not established except between two correlatives, so it is not perceived except by perceiving both of them. Thus the occurrence of coming as an action is not conceived except by perceiving an agent from whom the coming occurs and an object (p-551) upon which the coming occurs. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿he finds it to be nothing﴾ indicates the non-existence of a thing upon which the coming falls in His saying, exalted is He: "jaahu".

The answer to this is from two aspects, which Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir of this noble verse.

He said: If someone says, how is it said: ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾? If the mirage is not a thing, then what does the pronoun in His saying ﴿until, when he comes to it﴾ refer to? It is said: It is a thing that is seen from afar like the haze that is seen thick from afar; when one comes near to it, it thins out and becomes like air. It may also be that its meaning is: until, when he comes to the place of the mirage, he finds the mirage to be nothing, so the mention of the mirage was sufficient instead of mentioning its place. End of quotation from him.

The first aspect is more evident to me, and to him, by the evidence of his saying: "and it may be that its meaning is", etc. The end of our discussion in "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab." You have seen in it the answer of Ibn Jarir al-Tabari to the aforementioned question. His saying, exalted is He, in this verse: "biqi'atin" (in a level plain). It was said: it is the plural of qa'in (a flat ground), like jar and jirah; and it was said: qi'ah and qa' have the same meaning, and it is the level, even, wide expanse of the earth. Accordingly, qa' is the singular of qi'an, like jar and jiran.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾.

It is not hidden what comes to the mind regarding it, that the pronoun in His saying "jaahu" indicates an existing thing upon which the coming falls, because the occurrence of coming upon nothingness is not conceivable; and it is known that a relative attribute is not established except between two correlatives, so it is not perceived except by perceiving both. Thus the occurrence of coming as an action is not conceived except by perceiving an agent from whom the coming occurred. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿he finds it to be nothing﴾ indicates the non-existence of a thing upon which the coming falls in His saying, exalted is He: "jaahu".

The answer to this is from two aspects, which Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir of this verse. He said: If someone says: how is it said: ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾? If the mirage is not a thing, then what does the pronoun in His saying ﴿until, when he comes to it﴾ refer to? (p-355) It is said: It is a thing that is seen from afar, like the haze that is seen thick from afar, and the vapor; when one comes near to it, it thins and becomes like air. It may also be that its meaning is: until, when he comes to the place of the mirage, he finds the mirage to be nothing, so the mention of the mirage was sufficient instead of mentioning its place. End of quotation from him, in his exact words.

The first aspect is more evident to me, and to him, by the evidence of his saying: "and it may be that its meaning is", etc.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each already knows its prayer and its glorification. And Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

Know that the omitted pronoun, which is the subject (fa'il) of ʿalima ("knew"), some of the scholars (ahl al-ʿilm) said: it refers back to Allah in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah glorifies Him whoever is in the heavens﴾. On this view the meaning is: each of those who glorify and pray, Allah has known their prayer and their glorification. Other scholars said: the pronoun mentioned refers back to His saying "each" (kull), meaning: each of those who pray and glorify has known the prayer of its own self and the glorification of its own self. We have already presented, in the surah of al-Nahl, in discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 97], the statement of the usuliyyun (scholars of legal theory) that if an expression admits of both emphasis (tawkid) and establishing a new meaning (ta'sis), it is taken to mean establishing a new meaning, and we demonstrated many examples of this from the Mighty Qur'an.

Having known this, know that the more apparent reading, in accordance with what we have mentioned from the usuliyyun, is that the pronoun of the omitted subject in His saying: ﴿each already knows its prayer and its glorification﴾ refers back to His saying "each" (p-552), meaning: each of those who pray already knows the prayer of its own self, and each of those who glorify already knows the glorification of its own self. On this view, His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ is an establishing of a new meaning, not an emphasis. As for the view that the pronoun refers back to Allah, meaning: Allah has known its prayer, His saying ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ would be like a repetition alongside that, and thus would be of the type of verbal emphasis.

You have known that what is established in the usul is that taking an expression as establishing a new meaning is preferable to taking it as emphasis, as its clarification has already preceded. The apparent sense is that the birds glorify and pray, a prayer and a glorification which Allah knows, while we do not know them, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

Among the verses indicating that non-rational created things have a perception which Allah knows and we do not know is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning stones: ﴿And indeed among them is that which descends out of fear of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74], whereby He affirmed fear (khashyah) for the stones, and fear occurs through perception. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting apart from fear of Allah﴾ [al-Hashr: 21]; and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to carry it and feared it﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Ahzab: 72]. Refusal and fear occur only through perception. The verses and the hadiths are reported to this effect, and this is the truth. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the birds have prayer and glorification, and there is no barrier to taking it in its apparent sense. Al-Qurtubi transmitted from Sufyan that the birds have a prayer in which there is no bowing (ruku') or prostration (sujud). End of quotation.

It is known that salah (prayer) in the linguistic sense means supplication (du'a'), and from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"Mine daughter says, when I have set out travelling away: 'O Lord, keep my father far from ailments and pain.' Upon you is like what you have prayed (salaytī), so be content with sleep, for the side of a man has its resting place."

So His saying "mithla alladhi sallaytī" means: like what you have supplicated (da'awti), meaning her saying: "O Lord, keep my father far from ailments and pain."

His saying ṣāffāt means: spreading their wings in the air. Allah, may He be exalted, has clarified in another place that His holding the birds spread-winged in the air and folding them is among the signs of His power and of His right to be worshipped alone, and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 19], and His saying, may He be exalted: (p-553) ﴿Have they not seen the birds subjected in the air of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-Nahl: 79].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them﴾. In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, He mentions that He has promised those of this Ummah who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾, meaning He will surely make them the caliphs (khulafa') of the earth, those who hold authority over it and the enforcement of the word. The verses indicate that obedience to Allah, through faith in Him and righteous knowledge and action, is a cause of strength, of succession upon the earth, and of the enforcement of the word.

- Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away, so He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help﴾ [al-Anfal: 26],

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And with Allah is the outcome of all matters﴾ [al-Hajj: 40-41],

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you help Allah, He will help you and make your feet firm﴾ [Muhammad: 7],

along with other verses.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿just as He made successors those before them﴾, meaning like the Children of Israel.

Among the verses clarifying this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors. And We would establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas: 5-6]. And His saying, exalted is He, concerning Musa, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace: ﴿Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land and then observe how you act﴾ [al-A'raf: 129]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf: 137], along with other verses.

His saying, exalted is He: "la-yastakhlifannahum" (surely He will make them successors). The lam is a preparatory lam (lam al-muwatta'ah) for an omitted oath, meaning: Allah promised them and swore in His promise that He would surely make them successors.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾. This religion which He approved for them is the religion of Islam, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be in the Hereafter among the losers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85]. And His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: its "tamkin" (establishment) is its firm settling and consolidation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy﴾. This noble verse indicates that establishing prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger (ﷺ) are a cause of receiving Allah's mercy, whether we say that la'alla in His saying ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾ is a particle of causation (ta'lil) or of hope (tarajji). For if we say it is a particle of causation, then establishing prayer and what is conjoined to it are a cause of Allah's mercy, because causes (al-'ilal) are legal causes (asbab shar'iyyah). And if we say that la'alla is for hope, meaning: establish prayer and give zakah, hoping that Allah will show you mercy through that, then this is because Allah does not make them hope for that mercy, when they know its requirement, except that He will show them mercy, due to what is known of His bounty and generosity. The fact that la'alla here is for hope is only according to the knowledge of created beings, as we have explained in other than this place. And what this verse indicates, that if they establish prayer, give zakah, and obey the Messenger, Allah will show them mercy through that, is made clear in another verse, His saying: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another; they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy on them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71] — and His saying in this verse: "and obey the Messenger" after His saying "and establish prayer and give zakah", which is the conjunction of the general to the specific (ʿatf al-ʿam ʿala al-khass), because establishing prayer and giving zakah are included within the generality of His saying "and obey the Messenger". We have previously stated several times that conjoining the general to the specific and its reverse are both acceptable forms of elaboration (itnab maqbul) when the specific has a distinction not found in the other members of the general.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 57:**

God's words, ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape [Us] in the earth﴾. God forbade His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) from supposing, that is, from thinking, that those who disbelieve could escape [Him] in the earth. The object of *mu'jizin* (those who escape) is omitted, meaning: do not think that they can escape their Lord. Rather, He is able to punish them and cannot be prevented from doing whatever He wills to them, because He is capable of everything.

What this noble verse indicates is made clear in other verses, such as:

• God's words: ﴿And know that you cannot escape God, and that God will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawba: 2].

• God's words: ﴿And if you turn away, then know that you cannot escape God. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Tawba: 3].

• God's words: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 4].

• God's words: ﴿Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it is certainly true, and you cannot escape [it]"﴾ [Yunus: 53].

• God's words: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And you cannot escape [Him] in the earth or in the heaven﴾, to the end of the verse [al-'Ankabut: 21–22].

• His words in "al-Shura": ﴿And you cannot escape in the earth, and you have no protector or helper other than God﴾ [al-Shura: 31].

And other verses besides these.

As for His words in this noble verse, ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Nur: 57], Ibn 'Amir and Hamza recited it as *la yahsabanna* with the *ya'* (third person, masculine, the ghayb form). The rest of the seven readers recited it as *la tahsabanna* with the *ta'* (second person). Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Hamza read *sin* with a fatha (*hasiba*), while the rest of the seven read it with a kasra (*hasiba*, as the vowel of the verb's form).

The summary is that the recitation of Ibn 'Amir and Hamza is with the *ya'* and fatha on the *sin*; the recitation of 'Asim is with the *ta'* and fatha on the *sin*; and the recitation of the remaining readers of the seven is with the *ta'* and kasra on the *sin*. According to the recitation of those who read with the *ta'*, there is no difficulty in the verse, whether the *sin* is read with fatha or kasra, because the address in *la tahsabanna* is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the words *alladhina kafaru* ("those who disbelieve") are the first object, while *mu'jizin* is the second object of *tahsabanna*. As for the recitation *wa la yahsabanna* with the *ya'*, there is a well-known difficulty in the verse. Al-Qurtubi mentioned the answer to it in three ways:

The first: that His words *alladhina kafaru* are in the place of the nominative as the subject of *yahsabanna*, and the first object is omitted, its estimate being *anfusahum* ("themselves"), and *mu'jizin* is the second object. That is: "Let not those who disbelieve think themselves to be escaping God in the earth." He attributed this view to al-Zajjaj. The omitted object may be indicated by the recitation of the one who reads with the *ta'*, as is not hidden. The two objects of a verb of the heart (*fi'l qalbi*) may be omitted, or one of them may be omitted if there is evidence for it, as Ibn Malik indicated in his *al-Khulasah*, in his words:

> "Do not permit here, without evidence, the dropping of two objects or of one object."

An example of omitting both objects together while the evidence for them remains is God's words: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ [al-Qasas: 62], meaning: "whom you used to claim to be My partners." And the words of al-Kumayt:

> "By what book, or by what sunnah, do you see their love as a shame upon me, and you think [it so]?"

That is: "and you think their love a shame upon me." An example of omitting one of the two objects is the words of 'Antarah:

> "You have indeed come down, so do not suppose other than this of me, [that I am] to you as a loving, honoured [one]."

That is: "do not suppose other than this to be the case."

The second answer: the subject of *yahsabanna* is the Prophet (ﷺ), since he is mentioned in His words before it: ﴿Say: "Obey God and obey the Messenger"﴾. That is: "Let not Muhammad (ﷺ) think that those who disbelieve are escaping." On this view, *alladhina kafaru* is the first object, and *mu'jizin* is the second object. He attributed this view to al-Farra' and Abu 'Ali.

The third answer: the meaning is: "Let not the disbeliever think that those who disbelieve are escaping in the earth." He attributed this view to 'Ali ibn Sulayman. It is like the one before it, except that the subject in the first is the Prophet (ﷺ) and in the second is the disbeliever. Al-Zamakhshari said: "It was read *la yahsabanna* with the *ya'*, and in it there are views: that ﴿escaping in the earth﴾ are the two objects. The meaning: 'Let not those who disbelieve think that anyone can escape God in the earth, so that they hope for the like of that themselves.' This is a strong and good meaning. And that the pronoun of the Messenger may be in it, since he was mentioned before in His words: ﴿Say: 'Obey God and obey the Messenger'﴾. And that the original would be: 'Let not those who disbelieve think them escaping,' then the pronoun, which is the first object, was omitted. What made this permissible seems to be that when the subject and the two objects refer to one thing, one is content with mentioning two instead of mentioning the third." End of quotation.

As for what al-Nahhas, Abu Hatim and others mentioned, that the recitation of the one who reads *la yahsabanna* with the *ya'* is an error or a solecism (*lahn*), it is a discredited statement to which no attention is paid, because it is a canonical recitation of the seven, established with an establishment that cannot be challenged, and Ibn 'Amir and Hamza, from among the seven, recited with it, as has already been mentioned.

The most evident of the answers in my view is that ﴿escaping in the earth﴾ are the two objects, so the first object is *mu'jizin*, and the second object is indicated by His words ﴿in the earth﴾. That is: "Do not think that those who escape God are existing or present in the earth." And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 62:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will of them﴾.

This noble verse indicates that he (ﷺ) has the authority to grant permission to whomever he wills. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission?﴾ [at-Tawbah: 43], and the rest of the verse, seems to indicate otherwise.

The answer is clear, and it is that he (ﷺ) has the authority to grant permission to whomever he wills among his companions who were with him on a gathering matter, such as the Friday or Eid prayer, or congregational prayer, or a gathering for consultation, and the like. This is as He, exalted is He, explained in His saying: ﴿And when they are with him on a gathering matter, they do not leave until they ask his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will of them﴾ [an-Nur: 62].

As for permission specifically regarding staying behind from jihad, this is the matter in which Allah explained to His Messenger that the better course is not to hasten to grant permission until it becomes clear to him who is truthful in his excuse from the liar. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾ [at-Tawbah: 43].

Thus it becomes apparent that there is no contradiction between the verses, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another﴾. The scholars have various opinions regarding this verse, which go back to two views:

(p-556) The first: the verbal noun, which is "du'a'" (calling), is idafa (genitive construction) to its object, which is the Messenger (ﷺ). According to this, the Messenger is the one being called.

The second: the mentioned verbal noun is idafa to its subject, which is the Messenger (ﷺ). According to this, the Messenger is the one calling.

The clarification of the meaning according to the one who said that the verbal noun is idafa to its object: the meaning is, "Do not make your calling of the Messenger, when you call him, like your calling of one another. So do not say to him, 'O Muhammad!' addressing him by his name, nor raise your voices in his presence as some of you do with others. Rather, say to him, 'O Prophet of Allah! O Messenger of Allah!' with lowered voices, out of respect for him (ﷺ)."

This view is the one supported by verses of the Book of Allah, exalted is He:

• His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive﴾ and ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah - those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2-3],

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers - most of them do not reason﴾ and ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them﴾ [al-Hujurat: 4-5],

• And His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not say, "Ra'ina"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 104],

This view regarding the verse is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah, as al-Qurtubi mentioned from them. Ibn Kathir mentioned it from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, and also mentioned it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Muqatil, and he also reported it from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam. Then he said: this view is the apparent one, and he argued for it with the verses we have mentioned.

As for the second view, that the verbal noun is idafa to its subject, there are two interpretations of the meaning:

The first: what al-Zamakhshari mentioned in al-Kashshaf. He said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) needs you to gather with him for a matter and calls you, then do not disperse from him except with his permission, and do not equate his calling you with your calling one another, and your leaving the assembly without the permission of the caller.

The second interpretation: what Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir. He said: The second view regarding this is that the meaning of ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another﴾ is: do not believe that his supplication against others is like the supplication of others, for his supplication is answered, so beware lest he calls against you and you perish. (p-558) This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi. And Allah knows best. End of Ibn Kathir's words.

The author of these notes - may Allah pardon him and forgive him - says:

This last interpretation is rejected by the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, because His saying, ﴿like your calling of one another﴾, indicates the opposite. If He had intended their calling against one another, He would have said: "Do not make the calling of the Messenger against you like your calling against one another." The calling of some of them to some and the calling of some of them against others are different, as is not hidden. The apparent meaning is that His saying, ﴿Do not make﴾, is from "ja'ala" in the sense of "i'tqada" (to believe), as we mentioned from Ibn Kathir just above.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial should strike them or a painful punishment should afflict them﴾. The pronoun in His saying ﴿his command﴾ refers either to the Messenger or to Allah, and the meaning is one, because the command is from Allah, and the Messenger conveys it from Him. The Arabs say: "khalafa amrahu" and "khalafa 'an amrihi" (both meaning he opposed his command). Some said: "yukhalifun" is here given the meaning of "yasuddun" (turn away), i.e., they turn away from his command.

This noble verse has been used by the scholars of usul (legal theory) as evidence that a bare command, free of indicators, implies obligation, because He, majestic and exalted, threatened those who oppose His command with trial or painful punishment, and warned them against opposing the command. All of this implies that the command is for obligation, unless a diverting indicator turns it away, because what is not obligatory does not merit a severe threat and warning for its abandonment.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse, that an absolute command implies obligation, is also indicated by other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow﴾ [al-Mursalat: 48]. His saying "Bow down" is an absolute command, and His blaming those who did not comply with it, by saying ﴿they do not bow﴾, indicates that compliance with it is obligatory. Also His saying to Iblis: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12]. His rebuke of Iblis by saying ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ indicates that he abandoned an obligation, and that compliance with the command is obligatory, even though the command mentioned, namely His saying ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34], is absolute. Also His saying about Musa: ﴿Did you disobey my command?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 93], where He called opposition to the command "disobedience", and His command mentioned is absolute, namely His saying: ﴿Take my place among my people, reform, and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ [al-A'raf: 142]. Also His saying, exalted is He: (p-559) ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6]. The application of the name "disobedience" to opposing a command indicates that its opponent is a disobedient one, and one is not disobedient except by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act. Also His saying: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36]. This indicates that the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger prevent choice and necessitate compliance, and this indicates that it requires obligation, as you see. He indicated that opposing it is disobedience by His saying after it: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36].

Know that the language indicates that an absolute command requires obligation, by the evidence that if a master says to his servant, "Give me water," for example, and the servant does not comply with his master's command, and the master punishes him, the servant has no right to say, "Your punishment of me is injustice," because the form of the command in your saying "Give me water" did not make compliance obligatory upon me. You have punished me for abandoning what is not binding on me. Rather, it is understood from the very form that compliance is required of him, and that punishment for non-compliance is fitting.

As for the trial in His saying ﴿lest a trial should strike them﴾, it has been said that it is killing, reported from Ibn 'Abbas. It has been said that it is earthquakes and terrors, reported from 'Ata'. It has been said that it is an oppressive ruler, reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad. Some said it is the sealing of hearts because of the ill omen of opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). Some scholars said: a trial is a tribulation in this world. ﴿Or a painful punishment should afflict them﴾ in the Hereafter.

The author of these notes - may Allah pardon him and forgive him - says: Inductive study of the Noble Qur'an has shown that the word "fitnah" in it is used in four meanings:

The first: that it refers to burning with fire, such as His saying: ﴿The Day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who afflicted the believing men and believing women﴾ [al-Buruj: 10], i.e., they burned them in the trench of fire, according to the view held on that.

The second, and most famous of them: the use of "fitnah" to mean testing, such as His saying: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35], and His saying: ﴿And if they had remained on the way, We would have given them abundant water, that We might test them therein﴾ [al-Jinn: 16-17].

The third: the use of "fitnah" to mean the outcome of choice when it is evil, such as His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193], and in al-Anfal: (p-560) ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39]. His saying ﴿until there is no more fitnah﴾ means until no polytheism remains, according to the more correct of the two interpretations. The evidence for its correctness is His saying after it: ﴿and religion is for Allah﴾, because religion is not entirely for Allah while polytheism remains, as you see. This is clarified by his saying (ﷺ): "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no god but Allah," as is not hidden.

The fourth: the use of "fitnah" to mean proof (hujjah) in His saying: ﴿Then their fitnah was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23], i.e., their proof was not, as some scholars held.

What appears more likely to me is that the fitnah in His saying here, ﴿lest a trial should strike them﴾, is of the third type mentioned above.

Its meaning is that Allah tests them, i.e., increases them in misguidance because of their opposition to His command and the command of His Messenger (ﷺ).

This meaning is indicated by many verses of the Book of Allah, exalted is He:

• such as His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts with rust﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14],

• and His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5],

• and His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10],

• and His saying: ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is disease, it adds to them filth upon their filth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 125],

And the verses like these are many, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He knows what you are upon﴾. In this noble verse, He - exalted and majestic - makes clear that He knows what His creatures are upon, that is, of obedience and disobedience and other than that.

This meaning which this verse indicates, although it is known necessarily from the religion (ma'lum bi'l-darurah min al-din), has come explained in many verses:

• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you are not in any matter, nor recite from it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged therein. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register﴾ [Yunus: 61],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾ [Hud: 5],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then is He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned [like those who associate others with Him]?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 33], that is: He is a witness over His servants for what they do of good and evil.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful, who sees you when you arise, and your turning among those who prostrate. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 217-220],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is the same [for Him whether] one of you conceals speech or publicizes it, and whether one hides [himself] by night or goes forth freely by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And conceal your speech or publicize it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾ [al-Mulk: 13],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, and not a grain within the darknesses of the earth, and nothing fresh or dry but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am: 59],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All of it is in a clear register﴾ [Hud: 6],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14],

along with other verses besides these.

In these verses and what is in their meaning there is the best promise for the obedient and the most severe warning for the disobedient criminals. The particle qad (قَدْ) in His saying in this noble verse, ﴿Indeed, He knows what you are upon﴾, is for emphasis (lil-tahqiq). The use of qad for emphasis with the present tense (al-mudari') is very frequent in the Mighty Qur'an, like:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, clinging to one another﴾ [al-Nur: 63],

• And His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder [others]﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], the verse,

• And His saying: ﴿We already know that what they say saddens you﴾ [al-An'am: 33], the verse,

• And His saying: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky﴾ [al-Baqarah: 144], the verse.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [He knows] the Day they are returned to Him, and He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. His saying in this verse: ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾. The apparent meaning is that it is not an adverbial of time (zarf), but rather it is conjoined (ma'tuf) to the object (maf'ul bihi) which is "ma" in His saying: ﴿He knows what you are upon﴾, that is: and He knows the Day they are returned to Him. Allah, exalted and majestic, has mentioned in this noble verse that on the Day of Resurrection He will inform the creation of all that they did, that is, He will inform them of it and then recompense them for it.

What this noble verse indicates of His - exalted and majestic - informing them on the Day of Resurrection of what they did has come clarified in many verses, like His saying: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13], and His saying: ﴿And the register will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this register that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present. And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. The verses with the like of that are many, and Allah knows best.
